experiments.name: Heralded amplification of telecom time-bin and Fock-state qubits with 70%-efficient MoSi SNSPDs at 2.5 K in a closed-cycle cryocooler
experiments.plain_name: Boost a fragile light-based quantum bit sent through lossy fibre using super-cold photon counters
experiments.description: All-fibre heralded qubit amplifier at 1550 nm (Bruno et al., Geneva/NIST/JPL): four MoSi superconducting nanowire single-photon detectors (D1-D4) with 70% system detection efficiency, operated at 2.5 K in a two-stage closed-cycle cryocooler, register the 3- and 4-fold coincidences that herald the teleportation-based amplification.

requirements.rationale: The MoSi SNSPDs reach their 70% efficiency only at T < 2.5 K, so the detector stage must reach 2.5 K or below.
requirements.document_title: Heralded amplification of photonic qubits (Bruno et al., arXiv:1507.03210, 2015)
requirements.quote: We use MoSi SNSPDs with 70% detection efficiency at 1550 nm, at a temperature T < 2.5 K [27].

requirements.rationale: Each of the four nanowire detectors (D1-D4) must be current-biased and read out electrically to record the 3- and 4-fold heralding coincidences.
requirements.document_title: Heralded amplification of photonic qubits (Bruno et al., arXiv:1507.03210, 2015)
requirements.quote: The amplification is heralded by a 3-fold coincidence given by a click in the detector D1, which heralds the input photon, followed by D2 and D3, heralding its teleportation.

requirements.rationale: Optional: the detectors were designed for and operated in a two-stage closed-cycle cryocooler (no liquid-helium bath).
requirements.document_title: Heralded amplification of photonic qubits (Bruno et al., arXiv:1507.03210, 2015)
requirements.quote: The MoSi detectors were fabricated to obtain maximum efficiency at a wavelength of 1550 nm and for operation at 2.5 K in a two-stage closed-cycle cryocooler.

sources.citation: Heralded amplification of photonic qubits (Bruno et al., arXiv:1507.03210, 2015)

experiments.name: System detection efficiency of a NbN superconducting microstrip single-photon detector at 1550 nm at 0.84 K (adsorption refrigerator), with a 2.1 K G-M cryocooler cross-check
experiments.plain_name: Test a wide-strip superconducting photon counter below 1 kelvin so it catches over 90% of telecom photons
experiments.description: Xu et al. (SIMIT) characterise a fibre-coupled NbN microstrip detector (50 um active diameter) at two base temperatures: 0.84 K in an adsorption refrigerator, where the SDE reaches ~92.2% at 1550 nm, and 2.1 K in a compact closed-cycle G-M cryocooler (SDE > 70%). The detector is biased and read out through a cryogenic coaxial cable and a room-temperature bias tee.

requirements.rationale: The >90% system detection efficiency (near-saturated internal efficiency) was obtained at 0.84 K; reaching that temperature is needed to reproduce the headline result.
requirements.document_title: Superconducting microstrip single-photon detector with system detection efficiency over 90% at 1550 nm (Xu et al., arXiv:2101.05407)
requirements.quote: The SMSPDs are characterized at two different base temperatures: (1) 0.84 K in an adsorption refrigerator and (2) 2.1 K in a compact closed-cycle G-M cryocooler.

requirements.rationale: The detector is DC-biased and its RF pulses are read out through a cryogenic coaxial line to the bias tee.
requirements.document_title: Superconducting microstrip single-photon detector with system detection efficiency over 90% at 1550 nm (Xu et al., arXiv:2101.05407)
requirements.quote: The detector was then biased and read out through a cryogenic coaxial cable, connecting to a DC and RF output port of a bias tee (ZX85-12G-S+, Mini Circuit Inc.) placed at room temperature.

requirements.rationale: Optional: the paper also qualifies the detector (SDE > 70%) in a 2.1 K closed-cycle cryocooler, the practical deployment configuration.
requirements.document_title: Superconducting microstrip single-photon detector with system detection efficiency over 90% at 1550 nm (Xu et al., arXiv:2101.05407)
requirements.quote: Furthermore, the detector's SDE is over 70% when operated at a 2.1-K closed-cycle cryocooler.

sources.citation: Superconducting microstrip single-photon detector with system detection efficiency over 90% at 1550 nm (Xu et al., arXiv:2101.05407)

experiments.name: Coherent-one-way quantum key distribution over 250 km of ultra-low-loss fibre with NbN SSPDs at 2.5 K in a cryogen-free closed-cycle cryostat
experiments.plain_name: Send secret quantum encryption keys over 250 km of optical fibre using cold superconducting detectors
experiments.description: Stucki et al. (Geneva/Corning) run a 625 MHz COW QKD prototype over 250 km of SMF-28 ULL fibre; Bob uses two fibre-coupled NbN meander SSPDs operated at 2.5 K in a cryogen-free pulse-tube cryostat, biased at 26.5 uA for 2.65% efficiency at a 5 Hz dark-count rate.

requirements.rationale: The detector efficiency/dark-count trade-off used for the 250 km key exchange was characterised and operated at 2.5 K.
requirements.document_title: High rate, long-distance quantum key distribution over 250km of ultra low loss fibres (Stucki et al., arXiv:0903.3907, New J. Phys. 2009)
requirements.quote: Figure 3. Dark count rate vs detection efficiency at 1550 nm and 2.5 K.

requirements.rationale: Two SSPDs (data line and monitoring line) must be current-biased and read out electrically.
requirements.document_title: High rate, long-distance quantum key distribution over 250km of ultra low loss fibres (Stucki et al., arXiv:0903.3907, New J. Phys. 2009)
requirements.quote: In our experiment, over 250 km, we used this detector for the data line, with a bias current of 26.5 µA, leading to quantum efficiency of 2.65% at a very low noise rate of 5 Hz.

requirements.rationale: Optional: the prototype deliberately used a cryogen-free closed-cycle cryostat instead of the usual liquid-helium cooling for practical field integration.
requirements.document_title: High rate, long-distance quantum key distribution over 250km of ultra low loss fibres (Stucki et al., arXiv:0903.3907, New J. Phys. 2009)
requirements.quote: As part of the EU project SINPHONIA [11] we took a step towards their more practical integration and implemented these detectors in a cryogen-free, closed cycle, cryostat system (figure 2b).

sources.citation: High rate, long-distance quantum key distribution over 250km of ultra low loss fibres (Stucki et al., arXiv:0903.3907, New J. Phys. 2009)

experiments.name: Joule-class picosecond CPA with cryogenically cooled (77 K) Yb:YAG active-mirror amplifiers at 0.5-1 kW average power
experiments.plain_name: Amplify a kilowatt-class picosecond laser using crystals chilled by liquid nitrogen
experiments.description: Reagan et al. (Colorado State) amplify stretched pulses in Yb:YAG active mirrors cooled to 77 K by flowing cryogenic liquid; the 100-mJ stage sits on a cryogenic cooling manifold inside a vacuum chamber, and the joule-level stage uses 30 mm x 30 mm x 2 mm composite active mirrors, giving 1.5 J at 500 Hz and 1 J at 1 kHz.

requirements.rationale: The active mirrors are cooled to 77 K, where Yb:YAG becomes four-level with higher cross-section and thermal conductivity.
requirements.document_title: Scaling diode-pumped, high energy picosecond lasers to kilowatt average powers (Reagan et al., High Power Laser Sci. Eng. 6, e11, 2018, doi:10.1017/hpl.2018.3)
requirements.quote: The highly reflective face of the active mirror is cooled by direct contact with flowing cryogenic liquid cooled to 77 K[37].

requirements.rationale: The cryogenic cooling manifold carrying the gain medium is enclosed in a vacuum chamber.
requirements.document_title: Scaling diode-pumped, high energy picosecond lasers to kilowatt average powers (Reagan et al., High Power Laser Sci. Eng. 6, e11, 2018, doi:10.1017/hpl.2018.3)
requirements.quote: A 5 mm thick, 2 at. % Yb:YAG active mirror is mounted on a cryogenic cooling manifold enclosed in a vacuum chamber.

requirements.rationale: Free-space pump and seed beams must reach the cooled active mirrors and exit after each pass, so the cold enclosure needs optical windows.
requirements.document_title: Scaling diode-pumped, high energy picosecond lasers to kilowatt average powers (Reagan et al., High Power Laser Sci. Eng. 6, e11, 2018, doi:10.1017/hpl.2018.3)
requirements.quote: Seed pulses are injected into the amplifier though a thin film polarizer (TFP) and are directed to pass through each active mirror twice.

requirements.rationale: Joule-level active mirrors are 30 mm x 30 mm; the circumscribing diameter is 42.43 mm (rounded up to 42427 um).
requirements.document_title: Scaling diode-pumped, high energy picosecond lasers to kilowatt average powers (Reagan et al., High Power Laser Sci. Eng. 6, e11, 2018, doi:10.1017/hpl.2018.3)
requirements.quote: The active mirrors are composites, consisting of a 30 mm × 30 mm × 2 mm thick 3 at. % Yb:YAG section optically bonded on the four lateral faces to an absorbing Cr4+:YAG cladding

requirements.rationale: Optional: the source cools the Yb:YAG disks with liquid nitrogen; a cryocooler with sufficient lift at 77 K could substitute.
requirements.document_title: Scaling diode-pumped, high energy picosecond lasers to kilowatt average powers (Reagan et al., High Power Laser Sci. Eng. 6, e11, 2018, doi:10.1017/hpl.2018.3)
requirements.quote: For the 1 kHz operation we report here, the disk assembly was cooled by liquid nitrogen to 77 K.

sources.citation: Scaling diode-pumped, high energy picosecond lasers to kilowatt average powers (Reagan et al., High Power Laser Sci. Eng. 6, e11, 2018, doi:10.1017/hpl.2018.3)

experiments.plain_name: Measure how a laser crystal's light amplification changes as it is cooled from room temperature to 80 K

experiments.name: Operation of a fibre-pigtailed, bias-tuned quantum-dot micropillar single-photon source in a compact 2.4 K two-stage G-M cryocooler
experiments.plain_name: Run a plug-and-play fibre-connected quantum-dot light source inside a compact 2.4 K cooler
experiments.description: Margaria et al. (C2N/Quandela) directly attach a single-mode fibre to a deterministic QD micropillar whose p-i-n junction is bias-tuned through electrical contact ridges, then operate it in a rack-mounted compact two-stage Gifford-McMahon cryocooler at 2.4 K for ten-hour stability runs (fibre brightness 20.8%, indistinguishability 97.5%).

requirements.rationale: The pigtailed source was operated at the cryocooler base temperature of 2.4 K (the 5 K free-space setup gave lower indistinguishability).
requirements.document_title: Efficient fibre-pigtailed source of indistinguishable single photons (Margaria et al., Nature Communications 16:7553, 2025)
requirements.quote: After completion of the direct coupling process, the fibre-pigtailed source is installed in a compact two-stage Gifford-McMahon cryocooler operating at a base temperature of 2.4 K.

requirements.rationale: The QD charge state and emission wavelength are set by a bias voltage through electrical contacts on the chip.
requirements.document_title: Efficient fibre-pigtailed source of indistinguishable single photons (Margaria et al., Nature Communications 16:7553, 2025)
requirements.quote: For bias voltage tuning, each micropillar on the chip is connected to electrical contacts by four narrow ridges37 (Fig. 1a).

requirements.rationale: Optional: the deployable source runs in a closed-cycle G-M cryocooler without liquid cryogens.
requirements.document_title: Efficient fibre-pigtailed source of indistinguishable single photons (Margaria et al., Nature Communications 16:7553, 2025)
requirements.quote: We demonstrate the successful integration of our source in a compact two-stage Gifford-McMahon cryocooler operating at a base temperature of 2.4 K.

experiments.name: Atomic-frequency-comb preparation on Zeeman sub-levels of an Er:Ti:LiNbO3 waveguide at ~0.7 K and 3 kG (telecom quantum memory)
experiments.plain_name: Prepare a telecom-wavelength quantum memory in an erbium-doped crystal chip at 0.7 K inside a magnetic field
experiments.description: Askarani et al. (Calgary/Delft) cool a fibre-butt-coupled Er3+:Ti4+:LiNbO3 waveguide to about 0.7 K in an adiabatic demagnetization refrigerator, apply up to 5 kG along the c-axis, measure Zeeman-level lifetimes by spectral hole burning (350-800 G) and prepare 0.2-6.4 GHz atomic frequency combs at 1532 nm under 3 kG.

requirements.rationale: Long-lived Zeeman population storage requires spin-polarised Er ions at about 0.7 K.
requirements.document_title: Persistent atomic frequency comb based on Zeeman sub-levels of an erbium-doped crystal waveguide (Askarani et al., arXiv:1907.07780, 2019)
requirements.quote: which is cooled to a temperature of around 0.7 K using an adiabatic demagnetization refrigerator.

requirements.rationale: All AFCs were prepared under a 3 kG (300 mT) field along the crystal c-axis.
requirements.document_title: Persistent atomic frequency comb based on Zeeman sub-levels of an erbium-doped crystal waveguide (Askarani et al., arXiv:1907.07780, 2019)
requirements.quote: are created under the application of a 3 kG magnetic field (oriented along the crystal c-axis), and feature peak spacings of 50 MHz.

requirements.rationale: Optional: the setup exposed the waveguide to fields up to 5 kG (500 mT).
requirements.document_title: Persistent atomic frequency comb based on Zeeman sub-levels of an erbium-doped crystal waveguide (Askarani et al., arXiv:1907.07780, 2019)
requirements.quote: The waveguide is exposed to magnetic fields up to 5 kG oriented parallel to the c-axis of the crystal.

experiments.name: Miniaturised HTS bandpass-filter + cryogenic LNA receiver front-end operated at 71.8 K on a mini Stirling cryocooler (925 MHz)
experiments.plain_name: Cool a superconducting radio filter and amplifier to about 72 K for a compact telecom or radar receiver
experiments.description: Bian et al. integrate a YBCO-on-LAO HTS filter (925.2 MHz, 2.7 MHz bandwidth) and a cryogenic low-noise amplifier in a vacuum chamber cooled by a mini Stirling cryocooler of the type used for IR detectors; the microwave devices operate at 71.8 K using 0.325 W of cooling power.

requirements.rationale: The HTS filter and LNA were operated at 71.8 K.
requirements.document_title: A miniaturized HTS microwave receiver front-end subsystem for radar and communication applications (Bian et al., Physica C 2010), abstract
requirements.quote: The microwave devices inside the subsystem are working at 71.8 K with a consumed cooling power of 0.325 W.

requirements.rationale: The cold filter and LNA sit in an evacuated chamber on the cryocooler cold finger.
requirements.document_title: A miniaturized HTS microwave receiver front-end subsystem for radar and communication applications (Bian et al., Physica C 2010), abstract
requirements.quote: The whole front-end subsystem, including a HTS filter, a LNA, a cryocooler and the vacuum chamber, has a size of only φ 120 mm × 175 mm and a weight of only 3.3 kg.

requirements.rationale: RF input/output and LNA supply lines must reach the cold filter-amplifier chain to measure gain and return loss.
requirements.document_title: A miniaturized HTS microwave receiver front-end subsystem for radar and communication applications (Bian et al., Physica C 2010), abstract
requirements.quote: The center frequency of this subsystem is 925.2 MHz and the bandwidth is 2.7 MHz (which is a fractional bandwidth of 0.2%), with the gain of 19.75 dB at center frequency

requirements.rationale: Optional: the front end is cooled by a mini Stirling cryocooler, with no liquid cryogen, for field deployment.
requirements.document_title: A miniaturized HTS microwave receiver front-end subsystem for radar and communication applications (Bian et al., Physica C 2010), abstract
requirements.quote: This paper presents a miniaturized high performance high temperature superconducting (HTS) microwave receiver front-end subsystem, which uses a mini stirling cryocooler to cool a high selective HTS filter and a low noise amplifier (LNA).

sources.citation: A miniaturized HTS microwave receiver front-end subsystem for radar and communication applications (Bian et al., Physica C 2010), abstract

notes: Tavily quota was exhausted and the web-search budget ran out mid-task, so sources were read via direct PDF/HTML downloads (pdftotext) and WebFetch. The Thorlabs WDM qualification report could not be retrieved (page gated), so GR-1221 cyclic moisture (ESPEC GR-1221 page) replaces it; ESPEC table quotes are the table-cell texts joined in reading order. The JCU/Cryoelectra HTS cryogenic-receiver paper states no operating temperature, so the Bian et al. Physica C 2010 abstract (Consensus record URL; DOI not retrieved) is used instead. Fibre-coupled detector/source/memory profiles deliberately carry no optical_access requirement (optical_access = a window onto the sample; their light arrives by fibre). Minor glyphs (en dash, micro sign, multiplication sign, phi) were restored where pdftotext rendered replacement characters; the arXiv:1507.03210 'Detectors' quote is de-hyphenated across a line break.
